sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed side view, x/z gameplay with projected dimensional pixel rigs
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, Canvas 2D and Web Audio; full my-3D2dge 0.89.1, commit 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691; AI Hub protocol 1 / unchanged session client 1.4.0, commit 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Custom shaded procedural pixel art; coral and cream masonry, teal shutters, warm interiors and dusk skyline
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid and Blob continuous rigs, custom native E.Action window traversal, authored hazard state machines
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated chip music, synthesized effects and gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2-player AI Hub shared-world co-op with authoritative host/server; standalone solo and local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited headless checks allowed. One quiet verification command covers 41 rule scenarios, 4 transport scenarios, packaged Chromium/WebKit/Firefox, emulated controllers and multitouch, measured audio, and real Hub harness sessions. Physical-device play, human listening and first-player pacing: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original manual transcription, INTV Funhouse archive, MobyGames record, and a Games Database 30.2-second gameplay capture inspected as a motion strip. The source melody and human listening judgment are unknown.

testingFeedback: 23 distinct findings tracked across rule, browser, visual and contract verification; all fixed. These are defects/findings, not assertion counts.

4 were critical: tiny default canvas, inaccessible title controls, an undefined shutter-timing variable caught during an authoring refactor, and a stalled standalone fallback after a null Hub handshake. All were fixed before delivery.
Complete normal-intention routes plus the real multi-copy Hub harness: they exposed recovery, shared chances, replica movement and device-routing errors that a startup check missed.
Syntax-only checks. They were useful for parse errors but could not establish readable controls, fair collision or a complete rescue.
engineFeedback: The native Platformer already provides acceleration, jump cutting, buffering and coyote time. Humanoid/Blob rigs, Canvas lighting and Shell made a coherent game possible without external art.
I initially treated a null pad binding as automatic; it disables pads. Generic E.Action works with Platformer, but interactive hold/reverse needs explicit clock ownership.
The authoritative tower rules: timed shutters, encounter scheduling, shared hearts/chances, an idempotent award ledger, checkpoints, regrouping and the three-beat rescue.
Coordinating native physics and action ownership with client reconciliation, menu consumption and controller seat changes.
None in the vendored engine. Custom E.Action/shape/material registries, a native 8-unit PlatformMap grid, Shell styling and input-instance hooks implement the game. The Hub client is unchanged.
A documented interactive action hold/reverse API, with typed movement ownership and seat-reassignment examples, would make this integration easier.
promptFeedback: The distinctive source mechanics, complete ending and concrete delivery/testing contracts gave the game a clear identity.
The plan describes ultra effort while TASK specifies max. TASK supplied the authoritative metadata. Human seven-to-nine-minute first-run pacing cannot be established in this unattended environment.
Proving one coherent game across standalone, local co-op and an authoritative non-playing Hub server while packaging everything into a single offline HTML.
Separate required acceptance cases from suggested pacing targets and list the minimum reusable content schema up front.

aiHub.name: Beauty and the Falling Fool
aiHub.tagline: Love is a long way up.
aiHub.description: Climb the Mutton Building through timed shutters, jump Hank’s boulders, and catch Mabel’s hearts for a glorious rampage. Rescue her from the roof and leave by biplane, solo or with a climbing buddy.
aiHub.controls: Stick / WASD / arrows: move and climb; Cross / Space: jump; Options / Escape: menu; touch: left drag, right tap.
